entities.summary:
Daduhepa (b. 1400 BCE) was an economist or social scientist of the Classical era, active in Global. Known in the fields of monarchs & rulers, Daduhepa's contributions are significant within the context of the Bronze Age civilizations of Mesopotamia and Egypt.



Daduhepa's work in the field of economics and social science focused on the development of trade networks and the management of resources. He is particularly notable for his role in the establishment of the first recorded system of taxation in ancient Sumeria.



Daduhepa's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his ideas and methods were adopted and adapted by subsequent civilizations. The influence of his work can be seen in the development of modern economic systems and the role of governments in regulating the economy.



The impact of Daduhepa's work on the course of human history is evident in the continued relevance of his ideas on trade and taxation, which remain essential components of modern economic policy.
